outgroupPolarityBench.title: The baseline decides which traits are new
outgroupPolarityBench.subtitle: Nominate a starting point and re-read the same scores against it
outgroupPolarityBench.aria: Each character shown as the baseline state on the left and the novelty it polarizes to on the right, with bar length showing how many specimens share that novelty

kind.autapomorphy: Stranded on one specimen — groups nobody

readout.groupingNote: shared novelties you can build a branch on
readout.lonersNote: held by one specimen, so they say nothing

verdict.clean: A creature that branched off before the family gives the honest compass: carbon-threaded bone and the neural queue both read as novelties shared by everything else on the bench, and the whole bestiary gathers into one branch.
verdict.crestLost: Nominate a member of the family as the baseline and its own traits become the definition of 'ancestral'. The carbon bone and the queue go dark — everyone already has them, so they group nobody — and the family crest vanishes from the evidence without a single score changing. Worse, genuinely ancient anatomy gets promoted to a novelty, so the tree comes out confident and backwards.

hexapodGaitSequencer.title: Six legs are a timing problem
hexapodGaitSequencer.subtitle: When each foot is down decides support, spring, and the brace for a turn
hexapodGaitSequencer.ariaChart: Footfall chart showing when each of the six feet is on the ground across one stride
hexapodGaitSequencer.ariaBody: The direhorse seen from above with {feet} of six feet currently planted
hexapodGaitSequencer.stanceLegend: A lit bar means that foot is carrying weight
hexapodGaitSequencer.midPhaseLabel: Where the short middle pair lands

readout.braceNote: middle foot planted when the stride legs let go
readout.suspensionNote: both stride pairs clear of the ground

verdict.grounded: One of the long stride pairs is always carrying weight, so nothing about this gait is a leap. It is the cheapest gait to hold and the most punishing per step, because no tendon gets to store and return the energy of a bounce.
verdict.bouncing: The stride pairs now leave the ground together, and a middle foot is planted through almost every gap they leave. That airborne moment lets the long tendons work as springs — kinder on bone than a heavy walk — while the short pair still has purchase whenever a turn arrives.
verdict.unbraced: The middle pair is timed to swing at exactly the moments the stride legs have let go. Those are the instants a hard turn needs something planted to push sideways against, and the sideways brace is the job canon gives those middle legs.

pneumaticBoneBudget.title: Hollowing a wing bone, without losing it
pneumaticBoneBudget.subtitle: Same rigidity throughout — only the wall thickness and the material change
pneumaticBoneBudget.aria: Cross-section of a wing bone with its air channel, beside bars for the spar's mass and how close its wall is to crumpling
pneumaticBoneBudget.bucklingBar: How thin the wall has become

verdict.solid: A nearly solid spar is safe and heavy. Most of that material sits near the centre, where it barely resists bending at all — mass carried for nothing, and no channel for the air that has to cool a flying animal from the inside.
verdict.tuned: This is the bargain a flyer wants. The material has moved outward to where it actually resists bending, so the spar holds the same rigidity for a fraction of the weight, and the open middle becomes the duct that carries flight heat out of the skeleton.
verdict.fragile: The wall is now so thin that bending is no longer what breaks it. A tube this slender fails by crumpling locally, like a drinks can underfoot — and a wing spar that crumples at the wrong instant does not get a second stroke.
